title: RLTP Access Operation Envelope (transcription of Access Layer 0.54 section 3.3, envelopes rltp-access/0.25 and rltp-access/0.24)
description: TRANSCRIPTION, not the definition: the Access layer owns this shape; this schema exists so Membership Tasks and key-delivery validate payloads offline (Delivery Contract offline schema rule). Self-addressing id (oid: + base64url SHA-256 over the JCS serialization with id empty and proof omitted); every signature covers exactly that serialization. Root is OPEN (additionalProperties: true): per Access 3.3 unknown fields not named in crit MUST be IGNORED, so the schema passes them through — rejection of unknown restrictive extensions is the crit mechanism's job at the Access layer, never the schema's. Three proof mechanisms per Access 4.3. Body profiles per operation are transcribed in the if/then blocks (Access 4.5); bodies of unlisted registered operations validate as objects and are judged by materialization. New in 0.25 (Access 9.2, 11): keyOpDigest — the digest of the adapter's key operation — in the genesis body and in every transition (RLTP-ACC-9270, 7045, 4440); the transition carries the adapter's material binding, which for linear/0.1 is contentKeyCommitment, keyDist and the lineage choice (9.4.1), and for an adapter whose key operation travels beside the operation (beekem/0.1, 9.4.2) nothing beyond newEpoch and keyOpDigest; device.add and device.revoke bind and revoke device cards (Access 5.1); dag.join (additive, empty body) joins DAG heads beyond the prev bound of 32 (RLTP-ACC-3170, 3172); history.expose names each exposed key's key state under 0.25 (RLTP-ACC-8090). Both wire versions validate (RLTP-ACC-11100): the access-operation/0.1 task of the Membership Tasks is pinned to rltp-access/0.24, and a receiver accepts 0.24 and 0.25 until that pin advances; keyOpDigest is REQUIRED only under 0.25, and lineage takes the single-object form { opens: <epoch number>, ct } under 0.24 and the array of { opens: <operation id>, ct } under 0.25 (the conditional blocks at the end of allOf).

v.description: wire version: 0.25 is what Access 0.54 produces; 0.24 is accepted inside access-operation/0.1 until the companion's pin advances (RLTP-ACC-11100); keyOpDigest is required only under 0.25

prev.description: the op-ids of the DAG heads known to the author at authoring time, up to this bound of 32; where more heads are known, the 32 smallest in unsigned bytewise order, the omitted heads remaining heads to be joined by later operations (RLTP-ACC-3170) — dag.join, additive with an empty body, joins heads without any other decision (RLTP-ACC-3172)

items.description: complete vouch@1 artifact per Access 5.3 (the wire member keeps its 0.24 name); validated against access-vouch.schema.json by the consumer

card.description: the founder's contact card in the displayed form of Encounter section 6 (proof under its anchor = the founder; no sentTo/boundTo); its key-agreement key receives the founder's future keyDist envelopes

contentKeyCommitment.description: the epoch-0 binding of linear/0.1 (Access 4.5, 9.4.1): REQUIRED when adapter is linear/0.1

keyOpDigest.description: digest of the adapter's epoch-0 key operation as the adapter defines it (Access 9.2, RLTP-ACC-3260, 9270); REQUIRED under rltp-access/0.25, absent from the 0.24 form (RLTP-ACC-11100)

transition.description: policy.change is an enforcement operation (Access 4.5): a constitutional change carries its epoch transition atomically, which is what removed the same-base race and the suppression cascade (Access 3.6)

toEpoch.description: optional exclusive range end (default: the opening epoch E); fromEpoch < toEpoch <= E; keys covers exactly [fromEpoch, toEpoch), at most 4096 epochs per operation — longer histories compose from adjacent ranges (Access section 8)

keys.description: one entry per key state whose transition's newEpoch lies in [fromEpoch, toEpoch), at most 4096 entries, a span with more key states exposed in several operations (RLTP-ACC-8090, 8100); the entry shape is per wire version (the conditional blocks at the end of allOf): under rltp-access/0.25 { keyState, key }, under rltp-access/0.24 the bare key string

transition.description: the id of the transition whose lineage edge is re-published or bridged (RLTP-ACC-9830)

opens.description: the id of the transition whose key state the edge opens (RLTP-ACC-9830); the first canonical verifying entry per (transition, opens) counts (9820)

ct.description: AEAD ciphertext of the opened key state's content key under the content key of transition, AAD as in RLTP-ACC-9760

subject.description: the member anchor of the revoked device's person (Access 4.5)

device.description: the digest of the revoked device card (Access 4.5)

transition.description: device.revoke is an enforcement operation (Access 4.5, 5.1): the revoked device cannot derive the new epoch secret (RLTP-ACC-5160)

allOf.description: empty bodies (Access 4.5): member.leave (the subject is the author, 5.4), group.dissolve, dag.join (additive, no effect beyond its prev, RLTP-ACC-3172)
rltp-access/0.25: the genesis body carries keyOpDigest (RLTP-ACC-9270, 11100)
rltp-access/0.25: lineage takes the array form of RLTP-ACC-9760 with operation-id opens (RLTP-ACC-11100)
rltp-access/0.24: lineage takes the single-object form with an epoch-number opens (RLTP-ACC-11100)

key.description: the key of that key state in the form the group's adapter defines (linear/0.1: the base64url content key, 9.4.1), verified at materialization against the log's binding of keyState (RLTP-ACC-8090)

allOf.description: rltp-access/0.25: history.expose names the key state of every exposed key (RLTP-ACC-8090)
rltp-access/0.24: history.expose keys are bare key strings, the form of that wire version (RLTP-ACC-11100)

didKey.description: did:key over an Ed25519 public key; MUST additionally decode to multicodec ed25519-pub + 32 bytes (Encounter 2.3)

oid.description: self-addressing operation id: base64url(SHA-256) without padding over the JCS serialization with id empty and proof omitted

digest.description: multibase multihash (Encounter 2.3: producers emit u, verifiers accept u and z)

keyOpDigest.description: digest of the transition's key operation as its adapter defines it (Access 9.2, RLTP-ACC-7045, 9270); under linear/0.1 the multibase multihash over the JCS serialization of keyDist (9860); under beekem/0.1 over the key-operation bytes (9870); REQUIRED under rltp-access/0.25, absent from the 0.24 form (RLTP-ACC-11100)

contentKeyCommitment.description: multibase multihash over the RAW key bytes (Access 7.1 commitment rule), not over any JSON or base64url form; linear/0.1 only

keyDist.description: one entry per retained DEVICE: exactly the bound, unrevoked devices of the computed retained set (Access 7.1; linear/0.1 only, RLTP-ACC-9700, 9730), recipient = the device's did:key (a person's first device is its member anchor key, 5125), envelope = digest of the key envelope sealed to that device's key-agreement key (9740, 9750); recipients MUST be pairwise distinct (schema uniqueItems is object-level; the per-recipient uniqueness rule is normative text + vector). The 8 devices per member bound (RLTP-ACC-5145) is a validity rule, not a schema constraint.

lineage.description: linear/0.1 epoch-key lineage (RLTP-ACC-9760): the array form under rltp-access/0.25, the single-object form under rltp-access/0.24 (RLTP-ACC-11100); the version decides which (conditional blocks at the end of allOf)

historyNarrow.description: explicit narrowing act; requires the history.narrow aspect rule (default strongest) satisfied by this operation's proof in addition to the operation's own rule

lineageVoid.description: declared unbridged state, valid ONLY on a leave-discharging epoch.rotate (Access 7.1/5.4): the discharger holds no prior epoch key; ungated, surfaced as damage, under the standing repair duty of key-holding members; the discharge-only restriction is a materialization rule, not a schema rule

oneOf.description: linear/0.1 form (Access 9.4.1): contentKeyCommitment, keyDist, and exactly one of lineage, historyNarrow, lineageVoid (RLTP-ACC-9810)
form of an adapter whose key operation travels beside the operation (beekem/0.1, 9.4.2): newEpoch and keyOpDigest only

b64ct.description: base64url (unpadded) AEAD ciphertext incl. nonce and tag; minimum 80 chars = 32-byte key + 12-byte nonce + 16-byte tag

adapter.description: registered adapter identifier of the key port (Access 9.4, 11)

deviceCard.description: device card (Access 5.1): binds a FURTHER device to its person's member anchor; carries exactly these fields (RLTP-ACC-5110). A person's first device has no card: it is derived from the contact card of the genesis or the membership-accept (RLTP-ACC-5125). Proof = { signer, sig } per the 5.1 table: signer = the did:key of the signing device, a device of the same person bound and not revoked at the operation's position (RLTP-ACC-5120, 5175); sig = multibase base58btc (z…) Ed25519 signature over the JCS serialization with proof omitted. At most 8 bound, unrevoked devices per member (RLTP-ACC-5145) and the re-binding of a revoked device key (5175) are validity rules, not schema constraints.

anchor.description: the member anchor of the device's person in this group

device.description: the device's Ed25519 did:key, under which the device acts in the key port

keyAgreement.description: the device's X25519 key-agreement Multikey, to which key material for this device is sealed

opens.description: the id of the transition whose key state this entry opens (Access 9.4.1, RLTP-ACC-9705, 9760): a key state is named by its transition's id, never by an epoch number; a direct predecessor by default, an earlier one is the recovery form (9770)

ct.description: AEAD ciphertext of the opened key state's content key under this transition's content key, AAD = UTF-8 of JCS {genesis, newEpoch: <this transition's newEpoch>, opens: <the opened transition's id>} (RLTP-ACC-9760) — no own operation id in the AAD (hash-fixed-point rule)

lineage.description: rltp-access/0.25 form: linear/0.1 epoch-key lineage (RLTP-ACC-9760): one entry per key state this transition succeeds; a healing rotation carries one entry per open key state its author holds and surfaces the others as missing bridges (9762, 9780). Pairwise distinct opens is a validity rule, not a schema constraint.

opens.description: the epoch number of the previous epoch, whose transition this single edge opens (RLTP-ACC-11100)

ct.description: AEAD ciphertext of the previous epoch's content key under this transition's content key

lineage024.description: rltp-access/0.24 single-object lineage form: receivers MUST accept it as one edge opening the previous epoch's transition (RLTP-ACC-11100); valid only under v = rltp-access/0.24 (the conditional blocks at the end of allOf)

keyState.description: a key state's identifier: the oid: of the transition that created it (RLTP-ACC-9262) or an adapter merge identifier (RLTP-ACC-9264); never an epoch number (7042)
